previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, COPD, and polysubstance use, was admitted for shortness of breath and right toe pain. He had not taken his medications for four days due to homelessness. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic heart failure, worsening with volume overload, and ischemia of the right third toe with concern for embolic phenomena. He was treated with IV diuresis, transitioned to oral torsemide, and managed for atrial fibrillation with rate control using carvedilol and anticoagulation with Xarelto after ruling out HIT. Cocaine use was confirmed, prompting medication adjustments. Osteomyelitis of the second and third distal phalanges was diagnosed via imaging, leading to surgical disarticulation. He completed a course of cephalexin, and his wound healed well. He was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, improved volume status, and a plan for follow-up with cardiology, podiatry, and primary care.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
